# Volume 2 — XVII A Chapter of Accidents

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

During the night, Nell stirred from sleep thrice and journeyed to her window to ensure that the forecast from Uncle Zeb was not being fulfilled. At last, the daybreak arrived, pearl-like and bright within a firmament bursting with argent shimmer and brilliance, marking the arrival of the incredible day.
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0000 }

Isolde showed up shortly following breakfast, carrying a flower basket on one arm and holding her muslin dress over the other . . . since wearing it before finishing all the dinner preparations was out of the question. In the meantime, she was dressed in her afternoon pink print alongside a lawn apron that had fearful and wonderful ruffles and frills; moreover, she looked extremely neat, pretty, and rosy.
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0001 }

“You appear completely charming,” Nell said with admiration.
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0002 }

A sigh escaped Isolde.
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0003 }

“However, all of my dresses have required me to expand them once more. Compared to July, my weight has increased by four pounds. Where is this going to stop, Nell? Tallness and slenderness characterize every heroine created by Mrs. Varley.”
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0004 }

“Well, let’s ignore our problems and consider our blessings,” Nell said cheerfully. “According to Mrs. Wace, every time we recall something that tests us, we ought to likewise recall something pleasant that can balance it out. While you might be a bit too chubby, your dimples are most precious; and though my nose is freckled, its form is perfectly fine. Did the lemon juice help at all, in your opinion?”
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0005 }

“Indeed, I truly believe it achieved that,” Isolde remarked with a critical eye; and, feeling greatly pleased, Nell took the lead toward the garden, an area filled with delicate shadows and flickering beams of gold.
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0006 }

“The parlor will be decorated by us first. Plenty of time is available to us, because Honora stated their arrival would occur around twelve or half past at the latest, which means our dinner will take place at one.”
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0007 }

Somewhere in the United States or Canada, two girls might possibly have been more excited and happier at that instant, though I find it questionable. As peony and rose and bluebell dropped, each snip of the scissors appeared to twitter, “Mrs. Varley is coming today.” Nell was amazed that Mr. Pettifer was able to continue calmly cutting hay in the field over the lane, precisely as though no event was about to occur.
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0008 }

A somewhat austere and somber room was the parlor at Grey Shutters, featuring unyielding horsehair furnishings, rigid lace drapes, and white antimacassars that remained placed at an impeccably precise slant, save for those moments when they attached themselves to the buttons of unlucky individuals. For Thirza refused to allow any changes, meaning that not even Nell had ever succeeded in breathing much elegance into the place. Yet flowers can work amazing transformations provided they are granted an honest opportunity; after Nell and Isolde were done decorating the space, its identity would have been completely lost to you.
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0009 }

An abundance of snowballs spilled over a large blue bowl set upon the buffed table. Roses and ferns were piled high across the gleaming black mantelpiece. A cluster of bluebells rested on each shelf of the what-not; the dismal nooks flanking the grate were illuminated by jars packed with vibrant crimson peonies, while yellow poppies blazed within the grate itself. This entire display of magnificence and shade, combined with sunlight filtering through the window honeysuckle vines to cast a leafy flurry of dancing shadows across the floor and walls, transformed the ordinarily gloomy small space into the genuine “bower” of Nell’s fantasy, and further drew a nod of approval from Thirza, who had entered intending to fault but stayed to admire.
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0010 }

“It is time for us to arrange the table,” declared Nell, adopting the manner of a priestess preparing to carry out a holy ceremony for a deity. “A large vase filled with wild roses will sit at the midpoint, accompanied by a solitary rose placed before each person's plate—along with an exclusive arrangement made solely of rosebuds beside Mrs. Varley’s—which refers to ‘The Rosebud Garden’ as you are aware.”
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0011 }

The sitting room contained the set table, adorned with the highest quality china, glass, silver, and Thirza’s finest linen. You can be entirely sure that each single item put upon it had been scrubbed or buffed until it achieved the utmost achievable peak of shine and sparkle.
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0012 }

After that, the girls hurried out into the kitchen, a room overflowing with delicious scents coming from the oven, inside of which the chickens were already roasting delightfully. Nell took care of the potatoes, whereas Isolde made the peas and beans ready. Next, as Isolde locked herself in the pantry so she could mix the lettuce salad, Nell—her cheeks already starting to turn deep red, as a result of excitement just as much as the warmth from the stove—made the bread sauce intended for the chickens, chopped up her onions to go in the soup, and lastly beat the cream destined for her lemon pies.
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0013 }

And how was Robin faring throughout this period? Was he fulfilling his pledge to behave himself? Indeed, he was doing so. Of course, he maintained that he must stay in the kitchen, because his inquisitive nature demanded that he observe every single thing taking place. Nevertheless, since he remained peacefully in a corner, fully occupied with loosening the knots of a segment of herring net he had carried back from his previous visit to the beach, no person had any objection to it.
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0014 }

By eleven-thirty the lettuce salad had been prepared, whipped cream was piled high on the yellow rounds of the pies, and every item that was supposed to sizzle and bubble was sizzling and bubbling.
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0015 }

“We ought to go and change our clothes now,” Nell said, “because they could arrive by twelve. Dinner needs to be at one precisely, since the soup has to be brought out the moment it is ready.”
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0016 }

Grave indeed were the grooming rituals performed shortly thereafter within the eastern gable. Nell gazed with concern at her nose and felt glad upon observing that its freckles were not particularly noticeable, owing to either the lemon juice or the extraordinary glow upon her cheeks. By the time they were prepared, they appeared just as charming, neat, and youthful as any of “Mrs. Varley’s heroines” ever had.
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0017 }

“I do wish that I can speak occasionally, rather than remain silent like a dummy,” Isolde uttered nervously. “Every heroine created by Mrs. Varley speaks so wonderfully. However, I fear that I will become speech-blocked and foolish. Furthermore, I am certain to utter ‘I seen.’ I have not uttered it frequently since Miss Thorne served as a teacher here; nevertheless, it inevitably escapes during times of agitation. Nell, should I utter ‘I seen’ in front of Mrs. Varley, my shame would kill me. Moreover, remaining completely silent would be nearly as terrible.”
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0018 }

“There are a lot of things that make me anxious,” Nell remarked, “however, I doubt there is much danger of me being at a loss for words.”
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0019 }

And, to be fair to her, there was not.
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0020 }

Nell concealed her muslin finery beneath a large apron and descended to prepare her soup. Thirza, having dressed herself along with the twins, appeared more agitated than anyone had previously seen her. The Waces and Miss Thorne arrived when it was half past twelve. All was proceeding favorably, yet Nell started to experience anxiety. Honora and Mrs. Varley ought to have been there by then. She repeatedly walked to the gate, gazing down the lane with an intensity equal to that of her namesake in the Bluebeard tale watching from the tower window.
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0021 }

“What if they never arrive?” she asked with a pitiful tone.
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0022 }

“Do not assume that. It would be far too low,” stated Isolde, who, nevertheless, was starting to experience uneasy doubts regarding the matter.
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0023 }

“Nell,” said Thirza, emerging from the parlor, “Miss Thorne desires to look at Miss Pembroke’s willowware platter.”
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0024 }

Nell hurried over to the closet in the sitting room so that she could retrieve the platter. Following the pledge she made to Mrs. Sowerby, she had sent a letter to Miss Pembroke of Port Marlow to request borrowing it. As a longtime friend of Nell’s, Miss Pembroke dispatched the platter without delay, along with a note urging Nell to handle it with great caution, since it had cost her twenty dollars. After fulfilling its role during the Aid bazaar, the platter was placed back inside the Grey Shutters closet, because Nell refused to rely on anyone other than herself to carry it back to town.
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0025 }

Holding the platter with care, she brought it to the front entrance where those she was entertaining were taking pleasure in the refreshing air coming from the stream. After it was inspected and praised, a tremendous banging and rattling echoed from the kitchen pantry at the exact moment Nell received it into her hands again. Thirza, Isolde, and Nell rushed out, though the last woman paused just to place the valuable platter hurriedly upon the second stair step.
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0026 }

Upon entering the pantry, a genuinely dreadful sight confronted them . . . a young boy with a guilty expression clambering down from the table, his immaculate print blouse heavily smeared with yellow filling, while atop the table lay the broken ruins of what used to be two splendid, cream-topped lemon pies.
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0027 }

Robin completed untangling his herring net and rolled the cord into a sphere. Next, he walked into the pantry to place it on the ledge above the table, a spot where he maintained around twenty comparable spheres that, as best anyone could tell, fulfilled no practical function other than providing the pleasure of owning them. To accomplish this, Robin was required to step onto the table and stretch toward the ledge at a precarious slope . . . an action that Thirza had instructed him not to perform, given that he had previously met with disaster during such an attempt. His outcome on this occasion proved catastrophic. Robin lost his footing and tumbled heavily right onto the lemon pies. His fresh shirt was destroyed for the moment and the pies were destroyed forever. Nevertheless, it is a bad wind that brings no benefit to anyone, and the pig ultimately profited from Robin’s misfortune.
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0028 }

“Robin Farrow,” Thirza said, while she shook him by the shoulder, “did I not forbid you to climb up on that table again? Did I not?”
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0029 }

“I forgot,” Robin whined. “So many things have been forbidden by you that keeping track of every single one is impossible for me.”
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0030 }

“Indeed, you are to go up to the higher floor and remain there until the evening meal has passed. It may be that you will have them organized properly in your mind before then. No, Nell, do not ever think of pleading on his behalf. My reason for penalizing him is not that he ruined your pies . . . that occurred by chance. My reason for penalizing him is his refusal to obey. Off with you, Robin, I command.”
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0031 }

“Is there no dinner for me?” Robin cried out.
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0032 }

“Once dinner has finished, you may head downstairs and eat your meal in the kitchen.”
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0033 }

“Oh, all right,” said Robin, feeling a bit relieved. “I am sure Nell will keep a few good bones for me, right, Nell? Because you realize that I had no intention of landing on the pies. Listen, Nell, as long as they are ruined, is it okay if I bring a few of the scraps to my room?”
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0034 }

“No, no lemon pie for you, Master Robin,” Thirza said as she shoved him in the direction of the hall.
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0035 }

“What shall we do for dessert?” Nell asked, gazing with regret at the destruction and debris.
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0036 }

“Bring forth a jar of strawberry preserves,” Thirza offered by way of comfort. “The bowl still holds an abundance of whipped cream to go with it.”
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0037 }

When one o’clock arrived, neither Honora nor Mrs. Varley had appeared. Nell experienced intense distress. All the food had been cooked to perfection and the soup was precisely as it ought to be, although it could not be relied upon to stay that way for very long.
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0038 }

“I do not think they are coming after all,” Thirza remarked in an annoyed tone.
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0039 }

Nell and Isolde looked to one another’s eyes for solace.
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0040 }

When it reached half past one, Thirza once more came out of the parlor.
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0041 }

“Girls, we need to eat dinner. Everyone feels hungry, so there is no point in delaying further. It is obvious that Honora and Mrs. Varley will not arrive, and waiting longer makes nothing better.”
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0042 }

Lacking any remaining enthusiasm for the task, Nell and Isolde began to serve the meal.
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0043 }

“I doubt I can swallow even one bite,” Isolde remarked sorrowfully.
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0044 }

“Neither do I. However, for the sakes of Miss Thorne and Mr. and Mrs. Wace, I trust all will turn out well,” Nell remarked without enthusiasm.
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0045 }

As Isolde served the peas, she sampled a bite, causing a most unusual look to pass over her face.
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0046 }

“Nell, was sugar added to these peas by you?”
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0047 }

“Yes,” Nell stated, mashing the potatoes like someone who was expected to perform her duty. “A spoonful of sugar was added by me. It is what we always do. Is it not to your liking?”
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0048 }

“However, a spoon of it was also added by me as I placed them upon the stove,” Isolde stated.
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0049 }

Nell let go of her masher and sampled the peas as well. After that, she pulled a face.
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0050 }

“How terrible! It never occurred to me that you had added sugar, since I was aware that your mother never does so. Miraculously, I happened to remember it . . . it constantly slips my mind . . . which led me to quickly add a spoonful.”
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0051 }

“My guess is that there are simply too many cooks involved,” remarked Thirza, whose face bore a somewhat remorseful look as she took in this conversation. “Since I was absolutely sure you had never kept it in mind in the past, Nell, I didn't expect you to recall the sugar . . . and because of that, I added one spoon.”
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0052 }

Peals of laughter, one following another, reached the guests in the parlor from the kitchen, though the cause of the amusement remained unknown to them. No green peas, nonetheless, appeared on the dinner table that day.
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0053 }

“Well,” Nell remarked, regaining her composure while sighing as she remembered, “at least we possess the salad, and I believe the beans remain undamaged. Let us take the items inside and finish this task.”
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0054 }

It could not be claimed that the meal achieved any great social success. Efforts to rescue the situation were made by the Waces and Miss Thorne, while the usual calmness of Thirza remained without any obvious disturbance. However, owing to a mix of disappointment and the aftermath of their morning excitement, neither Isolde nor Nell was capable of eating or speaking. For the benefit of her visitors, Nell made a heroic attempt to participate in the talk; nevertheless, every bit of her vivacity had been temporarily snuffed out, and, despite her affection for Miss Thorne and the Waces, she was unable to prevent herself from reflecting on how pleasant it would be once all the guests had departed for home, allowing her to hide her fatigue and letdown within the pillows of the east gable.
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0055 }

An ancient adage exists which truly appears to be divinely influenced on occasion . . . “it never rains but it pours.” That day’s capacity for troubles had not yet been reached. Right when Mr. Wace had concluded giving thanks, a peculiar, threatening noise echoed on the staircase, resembling a firm, weighty item tumbling down step after step, culminating in a colossal crash at the base. Everyone rushed out to the hall. Nell uttered a scream of horror.
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0056 }

Down at the foot of the steps, a large pink conch shell was positioned in the middle of the broken pieces of what used to be Miss Pembroke’s platter, while at the head of the steps, a frightened Robin was kneeling, staring below with eyes wide open at the destruction.
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0057 }

“Robin,” Thirza said in a portending manner, “was it your intention to toss that shell down?”
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0058 }

“No, I never did,” Robin whimpered. “I was merely kneeling in this spot, as quietly as could be, so I could look at you people between the bannisters, when my foot hit that old item and knocked it down . . . and I’m so very hungry . . . and I really want you to just whip a boy and get it over with, rather than constantly dispatching him to his room so he loses out on all the enjoyment.”
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0059 }

“Do not hold Robin responsible,” spoken Nell, picking together the pieces using shaking fingers. “The blame rests on me. That platter was placed there by me and completely slipped my mind. My negligence has brought a fitting punishment upon me; yet oh, what is Miss Pembroke going to say?”
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0060 }

“Well, you know it was merely purchased by her, so it lacks the status of a family heirloom,” Isolde said, attempting to offer comfort.
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0061 }

Not long afterward, the guests departed, believing this to be the most considerate course of action, whereupon Nell and Isolde cleaned the dishes while conversing with an unprecedented lack of words. Subsequently, Isolde returned home suffering from a headache, and Nell, plagued by one as well, retreated to the east gable, remaining there until Thirza arrived back from the post office at sunset carrying a letter that Honora had written the previous day. Mrs. Varley had sustained such a serious ankle sprain that she was unable to depart from her room.
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0062 }

“Also, my dear Nell,” Honora expressed in her letter, “it grieves me deeply, yet I fear our trip to Grey Shutters is completely off, because once Aunty’s ankle has healed, returning to Toronto will be necessary for her. Her arrival there is required by a specific day.”
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0063 }

“Well,” sighed Nell, placing the letter onto the red sandstone step of the back porch, the spot where she sat as the dappled sky rained twilight down, “I perpetually considered it too good to be true that Mrs. Varley would actually arrive. Yet there . . . that remark seems as defeatist as Miss Eliza Pullen and I feel disgrace for saying it. When all is said and done, it wasn't too good to be true . . . occurrences equally good and much superior are coming true for me constantly. And I guess today's happenings possess a amusing aspect as well. Maybe once Isolde and I become aged and graying we will find ourselves able to chuckle about them. However I sense that I am unable to anticipate doing so prior to that time, because it has genuinely been a harsh disappointment.”
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0064 }

“You are likely to experience several additional and more severe letdowns than this one prior to finishing life,” remarked Thirza, whose genuine intention was to deliver consoling words. “It appears to me, Nell, as though you will not ever abandon your habit of placing your hopes so intensely on matters and subsequently plunging into hopelessness when you fail to obtain them.”
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0065 }

“I am aware that I have too much of a tendency toward that,” Nell conceded with regret. “Whenever I expect something good to occur, I appear to soar straight up on anticipation’s wings; and subsequently, before I know it, I hit the ground with a bang. However, Thirza, the soaring portion is truly magnificent while it endures . . . it resembles floating across a sunset. I believe it nearly makes up for the bang.”
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0066 }

“Well, perhaps it is so,” Thirza conceded. “I would prefer to proceed at a peaceful pace and forego both the flight and the crash. However, each person possesses her unique manner of existence . . . It was once my belief that a single correct path existed . . . yet my confidence in that has waned since I was tasked with raising you and the twins. How do you intend to handle Miss Pembroke’s platter?”
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0067 }

“Reimburse her the twenty dollars she gave for it, I guess. I am extremely grateful it was not a prized heirloom since no amount of cash would be able to substitute for it then.”
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0068 }

“Perhaps you might discover a similar item in some place and purchase it on her behalf.”
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0069 }

“Regrettably, that is not the case. Platters from that era are extremely rare. For the supper, Mrs. Sowerby was unable to locate one at all. I truly wish I were able to, because Miss Pembroke, naturally, would be just as happy with any platter, provided both shared the same age and authenticity. Thirza, observe that large star above the maple grove belonging to Mr. Pettifer, surrounded by such a sacred stillness of silvery sky. A sensation resembling a prayer comes over me from it. Ultimately, when stars and skies of that nature are visible to us, minor disappointments and mishaps cannot hold so much importance, can they?”
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0070 }

“Where’s Robin?” asked Thirza, casting a casual look toward the star.
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0071 }

“In bed. I’ve pledged that tomorrow I will bring him and Lucy to the beach for an outing. To be sure, he was required to behave well under our initial deal. Nevertheless, he attempted to behave . . . and disappointing him was more than I had the heart to do.”
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0072 }

“Rowing on the pond in that punt will cause your death or the twins’,” Thirza complained. “Sixty years I’ve resided in this place, and not once have I gone out on the pond.”
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0073 }

“Indeed, a situation can always be rectified,” Nell stated playfully. “Imagine joining us on the morrow. Grey Shutters will be locked by us, and we will pass all twenty-four hours on the beach, putting all our cares behind us.”
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0074 }

“No, thank you,” Thirza said, emphasizing her words indignantly. “Wouldn't I look like a fine sight, taking a flat across the pond? I can almost hear Agatha commenting about it. Look at Mr. Pettifer driving off over there. Is there any truth, do you think, to the rumor that Mr. Pettifer intends to visit Isabella Pullen?”
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0075 }

“No, I am certain there is not. He merely dropped by one night to discuss business matters with Mr. Gorham Pullen, and Mrs. Sowerby spotted him, remarking that she was sure he was courting since he was wearing a white collar. I do not think Mr. Pettifer will ever get married. He appears to hold a bias against matrimony.”
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0076 }

“Indeed, predicting the actions of those lifelong bachelors is impossible. Furthermore, provided he wore a white collar, I would concur with Agatha regarding its suspicious appearance, because I am certain nobody ever caught sight of him wearing one previously.”
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0077 }

“I believe the sole reason he wore it was his desire to finalize a business arrangement with Gorham Pullen,” Nell remarked. “I have listened to him state that such an occasion is the single moment a man must pay close attention to his attire, since appearing wealthy makes the second party less inclined to attempt to defraud him. My heart truly goes out to Mr. Pettifer; I doubt he experiences any contentment in his existence. Living with nobody to love besides a parrot has got to be extremely solitary, wouldn't you say? However, I observe that Mr. Pettifer resents being the object of pity. No person enjoys it, I suppose.”
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0078 }

“Hugh is walking up the lane,” Thirza said. “Put on your rubbers and coat if he asks you to row on the pond. Tonight the dew is heavy.”
{: #nw-v02-c17-p0079 }
